I added `Cart.apply_coupon(code)` and the coupons now come off the subtotal in `calc_total`. All 13 tests pass (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`). I delegated the work to a sub-agent, then checked the changed files and re-ran the tests myself. I haven't read the new code line by line, and nothing is committed.

**What changed:**
- **`shop/coupons.py` (new):** holds the two coupons. SAVE10 takes 10% off and FLAT500 takes 500 cents off. Looking up an unknown code raises `ValueError`.
- **`shop/models.py`:** `Cart` now keeps a list of applied coupons and has `apply_coupon(code)`. An unknown code raises `ValueError` and leaves the cart as it was.
- **`shop/pricing.py`:** `calc_total` and `calc_tax` both take coupons into account.
- **`tests/test_coupons.py` (new):** 7 tests covering each coupon alone, both stacked, an unknown code, tax after a discount, and the total not going below zero.

**Choices you may want to change:**
- **Stacking:** each coupon's discount is worked out from the same subtotal, so order doesn't matter. On a 10,000¢ subtotal you get 1,000 + 500 off.
- **Bulk discount:** the cart already had a bulk discount. Coupons are applied after it, so SAVE10 takes 10% of the already-reduced amount.
- **Applying the same code twice:** the second time is ignored, so each coupon counts once.
- **Rounding:** the 10% is rounded half up to whole cents, using the same rounding as the rest of the money code.
- **Floor:** the discounted subtotal can't go below 0.
- **Tax:** only some items are taxable. The taxable amount is reduced by the same proportion as the whole subtotal, then the 8.25% rate is applied. This is the choice I'd most want you to check, since you might prefer to discount only the non-taxable items, or only the taxable ones.

You'll also see untracked `__pycache__/` folders from the test run in `git status`.
